decisions.reason: Changing the monthly quota from 125 to 100 does not alter which clips are eligible for publication or the assigned Instagram destination.
The requalification batch is a separate task-local assignment completed before the monthly production arrangement; its clip count and acceptance condition remain unchanged.
The numerical quota changes, but the client-personal approval authority, counting rule, and publication gate remain unchanged.
The monthly clip-count change does not modify the clean editing style or effects policy.
The source-material and moment-selection rules for the task-local requalification batch are unaffected by the later monthly quota.
Reducing the monthly approved-clip target does not change the requirement that each clip contain a complete, educational, standalone moment.
The completed task-local extended trial remains defined as 15 to 20 clips; the new monthly production quota does not retroactively modify it.
The completed initial three-clip trial is historically and semantically separate from the monthly approved-clip quota.
The quota reduction does not change the requirement to track every published clip or its views, performance, and engagement.
The monthly quota change does not alter the requirement to provide a dedicated Instagram account.
The numerical production quota has no effect on caption color, font, or text-effects requirements.
The change from 125 to 100 approved clips per month does not modify the required 30-to-90-second duration range.
